External links for this lesson, checked to load on 2026-11-13. Quoted regulatory and program text in
the lesson comes from the local copies in `sources/`, not from these pages.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.160, Records](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)** —
  the BECS records rule, including 606.160(c) on the donor number. Use it when anyone asks whether the
  extract changes what a record is. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 11.10, Controls for closed systems](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the controls that stay attached to the BECS records. Contrast, not a requirement for the extract.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.514, Other requirements relating to uses and disclosures of PHI](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514)**
  — the minimum-necessary paragraph (d) and, later in the same section, the de-identification and
  limited-data-set paragraphs module 3 relies on. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (CSRC publication page)](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)**
  — the voluntary control catalog; read CM-3 and CM-5 for the change-control vocabulary. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP, Questions and Answers](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-integrity-and-compliance-drug-cgmp-questions-and-answers)**
  — drug-CGMP guidance, not a blood-establishment rule. Use it only for general thinking about
  complete, consistent and accurate data. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[OMOP Common Data Model (OHDSI documentation)](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/)**
  — the model the 2022 paper says the V2V database is based on (it names v6). Use it to read the
  tables the DCC maps into. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[The Book of OHDSI, Chapter 6: Extract Transform Load](https://ohdsi.github.io/TheBookOfOhdsi/ExtractTransformLoad.html)**
  — the OMOP community's practical walk through mapping source data to the model. Read it to follow
  the DCC's side of the conversation. It describes OHDSI practice, not the REDS DCC's process.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[2017 OHDSI CDM & Vocabulary Tutorial (1 of 5)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BExsHYxkvTw)**
  (OHDSI, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the embedded video; general OMOP background, not about blood
  centers or REDS. I confirmed only its title and that it is one of five parts on the OHDSI
  [tutorial page](https://www.ohdsi.org/2017-tutorials-omop-common-data-model-and-standardized-vocabularies/)
  (HTTP 200); I did not watch it. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13.

## Keep learning

Not official sources, and not authority for any regulatory claim.

- **[OHDSI Data Quality Dashboard](https://ohdsi.github.io/DataQualityDashboard/)** (OHDSI, open
  source) — a practical catalog of field-level and conformance checks on OMOP data. Mine it for
  ideas for EXT-21's QC checklist and to understand what the DCC's checks may resemble. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[The Twelve-Factor App: Dev/prod parity](https://12factor.net/dev-prod-parity)** (practitioner
  essay) — why test and production should differ as little as possible; useful for the first-test-run
  discussion. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[OHDSI: Data Standardization](https://www.ohdsi.org/data-standardization/)** (OHDSI community) —
  the community's overview of its data standards, a gentle starting point before the CDM docs.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[The Book of OHDSI](https://ohdsi.github.io/TheBookOfOhdsi/)** (OHDSI) — the full free book;
  chapters on the CDM and data quality sit alongside the ETL chapter above. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
